# n9 - RoadmapQueue reads the shared model

Added at the plan review (A7). `RoadmapQueue#frontier_for` is refactored onto `RoadmapGraph`, and
the second roadmap-graph reader, the second topological sort, the second unnamed-entry fold, and
the second unlisted-id report inside `roadmap_queue.rb` are deleted. Without this node D1 is false
the day it ships: the screens would render batches from `ReadySet` while `roadmap-next` dispatched
from `topological_layers`, two sorts that agree today only by coincidence.

## n9 failure-mode matrix
| Row | Operation | Failure mode | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 9.1 | Delete `RoadmapQueue#topological_layers` and take batches from the shared model | Two topological sorts survive in one tree, the screens and the dispatcher can disagree about which batch an entry is in, and D1 is false | `roadmap_queue_graph_test#test_roadmap_queue_defines_no_topological_sort_of_its_own` |
| 9.2 | Delete `RoadmapQueue#parse_roadmap_graph` and read edges through the shared model | A second `## Graph` reader survives, so a fix to the exact-heading rule or the fence rule has to be made twice and will eventually be made once | `roadmap_queue_graph_test#test_roadmap_queue_parses_no_graph_section_of_its_own` |
| 9.3 | Keep the `queue`, `which`, and `roadmap` payload contracts byte-identical for every acyclic roadmap | The auto loop and the dashboard both read this payload; a renamed or dropped key breaks dispatch across every store at once | `roadmap_queue_graph_test#test_payload_is_unchanged_for_every_live_roadmap_fixture` |
| 9.4 | Keep the wave-order fallback for a roadmap with no graph | Twenty-one graphless live roadmaps lose their frontier the moment this lands, before the migration has run | `roadmap_queue_graph_test#test_graphless_roadmap_keeps_wave_order_frontier` |
| 9.5 | Keep the unlisted-id report the graph path already produces | An id the graph names that no batch lists goes back to being swallowed, and a queued entry sits forever with nothing in the payload explaining why | `roadmap_queue_graph_test#test_unlisted_graph_id_is_still_reported_in_blocked` |
| 9.6 | Keep the cyclic-roadmap error state and add the whole path | A cyclic roadmap silently returns a frontier again, which is the regression the shared cycle check exists to prevent | `roadmap_queue_graph_test#test_cyclic_roadmap_still_returns_error_state_with_the_whole_path` |
| 9.7 | Preserve the injected ranker seam and its default | The refactor bypasses `@ranker`, and the intent-173 ranking-swap seam silently stops being a seam | `roadmap_queue_graph_test#test_injected_ranker_still_orders_the_dispatchable_queue` |
| 9.8 | Keep roadmap file order within a batch before ranking | Folded at review (A8, D11): the shared model sorts a layer lexically, and rank 1 on `chat-shell-maturity.md` flips from `5` to `2`, changing what the auto loop dispatches next | `roadmap_queue_graph_test#test_dispatchable_order_matches_roadmap_file_order_within_a_batch` |
| 9.9 | Keep the existing `roadmap_queue_test.rb` and `roadmap_queue_graph_test.rb` suites green unchanged | The refactor is proven only by new tests written to match the new code, which proves nothing about the behavior that shipped | `roadmap_queue_test` and `roadmap_queue_graph_test` (existing, must stay green with no assertion loosened) |

## Steps
1. Red: the matrix's tests above, committed before any code in this node.
2. Write the code that makes them pass, deleting the duplicated readers rather than wrapping them.
3. Green, then `ruby bin/test` at its baseline before the next node starts.
